scope: General AI, software, business, operations, content, and media-production workflows represented by this catalog. Provider-specific duties, tool-only procedures, and work that legally or safely requires a qualified human remain outside Agent coverage.
criteria: Each catalog category declares the core work it is expected to route.
Each category names at least two existing representative Agents from that category.
Each category declares its normal downstream handoff.
Each category declares a boundary that prevents coverage from being interpreted as unlimited authority.

categories.coreWork: Frame decision questions, analyze quantitative or qualitative evidence, test assumptions, and communicate findings.
categories.handoff: Evidence, uncertainty, and recommendations pass to strategy, product, finance, or operations owners.
categories.boundary: Analysis does not authorize the resulting business, financial, or operational action.

categories.coreWork: Define system boundaries, interfaces, data structures, quality attributes, tradeoffs, and migration direction.
categories.handoff: Approved decisions and constraints pass to implementation, platform, security, and quality owners.
categories.boundary: Architecture proposals do not silently replace product requirements or production approval.

categories.coreWork: Design AI capabilities, prompts, evaluations, safety checks, model choices, and agent or MCP integrations.
categories.handoff: Evaluated capability contracts pass to product, development, security, and operations owners.
categories.boundary: Model output is not treated as verified truth or consequential approval without required evidence and human gates.

categories.coreWork: Plan operating processes, organizational change, procurement, partnerships, pricing inputs, and workforce enablement.
categories.handoff: Approved operating plans pass to accountable department, finance, legal, people, and delivery owners.
categories.boundary: Agents do not sign contracts, make employment decisions, or commit organizational resources.

categories.coreWork: Design and operate cloud, network, compute, container, service-mesh, infrastructure-as-code, and cost controls.
categories.handoff: Reviewed infrastructure plans and changes pass to security, operations, release, and service owners.
categories.boundary: Production mutation, credential use, and spend changes require the environment's authorization and rollback controls.

categories.coreWork: Plan and review storefront operations, catalog or order flows, checkout, and payment integration.
categories.handoff: Validated commerce requirements pass to product, development, finance, security, and customer operations.
categories.boundary: Agents do not move funds, issue refunds, change live prices, or bind a merchant without authorization.

categories.coreWork: Set creative direction, research attributable visual references, and create governed image concepts or assets.
categories.handoff: Approved direction and assets pass to design, marketing, media-production, and rights owners.
categories.boundary: References do not confer reuse rights, and generated assets do not bypass brand, consent, or provenance review.

categories.coreWork: Triage support needs, draft responses, track cases, identify adoption risks, and plan customer-success follow-up.
categories.handoff: Cases and account evidence pass to authorized support, product, sales, billing, or incident owners.
categories.boundary: Agents do not promise compensation, disclose private account data, or make binding account changes.

categories.coreWork: Model, ingest, transform, govern, query, administer, and retrieve structured, spatial, and vector data.
categories.handoff: Trusted datasets, contracts, lineage, and findings pass to analysis, ML, application, and governance owners.
categories.boundary: Data access, destructive changes, retention, and sensitive-data use remain subject to explicit policy and authorization.

categories.coreWork: Improve onboarding, local workflows, toolchains, dependencies, platforms, documentation paths, and developer feedback loops.
categories.handoff: Validated workflow improvements pass to maintainers, platform teams, documentation, and release owners.
categories.boundary: Convenience changes do not override repository policy, security controls, compatibility, or release gates.

categories.coreWork: Implement, debug, refactor, and maintain frontend, backend, mobile, desktop, systems, language, and framework code.
categories.handoff: Working changes and implementation evidence pass to review, testing, security, documentation, and release owners.
categories.boundary: Implementation remains constrained by approved scope, repository guidance, tests, and production authorization.

categories.coreWork: Design documentation systems and produce API, architecture, reference, tutorial, and diagram artifacts.
categories.handoff: Versioned documentation passes to maintainers, users, reviewers, and release owners.
categories.boundary: Documentation does not invent unsupported product behavior or replace verification against the implementation.

categories.coreWork: Analyze firmware and design or debug ARM Cortex embedded behavior, interfaces, timing, memory, and hardware constraints.
categories.handoff: Findings and implementation constraints pass to authorized firmware, hardware, security, and validation owners.
categories.boundary: Hardware flashing, safety-critical control, and proprietary reverse engineering require explicit authorization and qualified review.

categories.coreWork: Prepare accounting-control evidence, close readiness, forecasts, budgets, scenarios, and management variance analysis.
categories.handoff: Traceable analyses and proposed actions pass to authorized finance, audit, tax, legal, and executive owners.
categories.boundary: Agents do not post entries, move funds, file taxes, attest controls, or make fiduciary decisions.

categories.coreWork: Identify obligations, assess risk and compliance evidence, define policy controls, and review licensing or legal issues.
categories.handoff: Findings, exceptions, and control proposals pass to accountable legal, compliance, security, and business owners.
categories.boundary: Agent analysis is not legal advice, certification, regulatory filing, or final risk acceptance.

categories.coreWork: Review clinical evidence and data governance, patient-safety signals, preparedness, health information, and compliance workflows.
categories.handoff: Evidence and escalations pass to qualified clinicians, safety, privacy, regulatory, and operational owners.
categories.boundary: Agents do not diagnose, prescribe, triage emergencies, make care decisions, or replace qualified clinical judgment.

categories.coreWork: Develop, deploy, monitor, validate, and govern machine-learning models and pipelines.
categories.handoff: Validated models, evaluation evidence, and operational requirements pass to product, AI, data, security, and operations owners.
categories.boundary: A model is not production-approved solely because training or offline evaluation completed.

categories.coreWork: Plan, produce, measure, audit, optimize, and publish governed content, SEO, paid, and social campaigns.
categories.handoff: Approved content and measurement evidence pass to brand, channel, sales, legal, and publication owners.
categories.boundary: Publishing, spend, tracking, and claims require explicit channel authorization, rights, and compliance review.

categories.coreWork: Route research, direction, writing, planning, live capture, asset custody, editing, finishing, localization, accessibility, mastering, and delivery.
categories.handoff: Versioned media artifacts move through approval gates from brief and production lock to picture, finishing, locale, accessibility, and delivery locks.
categories.boundary: Qualified humans retain live-set, safety, consent, linguistic, legal, publication, and other specialist authority.

categories.coreWork: Deploy, observe, troubleshoot, respond to incidents, verify service health, manage reliability, and coordinate operational recovery.
categories.handoff: Verified changes, telemetry, incident state, and recovery evidence pass to service, security, release, and business owners.
categories.boundary: Production actions follow explicit authorization, least privilege, rollback, communication, and incident-command rules.

categories.coreWork: Plan multi-agent execution, allocate bounded ownership, manage context, implement coordinated work, and validate receipts.
categories.handoff: Scoped tasks and evidence converge into one accountable result for the requesting user or workflow owner.
categories.boundary: Delegation does not broaden authority, bypass approvals, or permit overlapping writes without coordination.

categories.coreWork: Measure and optimize application, system, query, schema, and database performance against explicit budgets.
categories.handoff: Benchmarks, bottlenecks, proposed changes, and regression evidence pass to development, data, and operations owners.
categories.boundary: Optimization does not trade away correctness, security, durability, accessibility, or cost controls without approval.

categories.coreWork: Discover needs, define outcomes and requirements, prioritize scope, write product specifications, and align technical delivery.
categories.handoff: Approved problems, requirements, priorities, and acceptance criteria pass to design, architecture, development, and project owners.
categories.boundary: Agents do not silently make executive prioritization, budget, roadmap, or market commitments.

categories.coreWork: Plan delivery, dependencies, milestones, risks, decisions, releases, communication, and closeout.
categories.handoff: Current plans, blockers, approvals, and release evidence pass among product, implementation, operations, and stakeholders.
categories.boundary: Schedules do not override quality, safety, labor, security, compliance, or accountable-owner decisions.

categories.coreWork: Design and execute tests, review code and UI, verify receipts, resolve review feedback, and make evidence-based quality recommendations.
categories.handoff: Findings, test evidence, accepted exceptions, and gate recommendations pass to implementation and release owners.
categories.boundary: Passing static checks alone does not prove user acceptance, production safety, or authorization to release.

categories.coreWork: Search authoritative sources, gather market or topic evidence, compare alternatives, record provenance, and communicate uncertainty.
categories.handoff: Source-backed findings and unresolved questions pass to analysis, strategy, product, content, or specialist owners.
categories.boundary: Research does not grant reuse rights or convert uncertain evidence into verified fact.

categories.coreWork: Prepare technical discovery, solution evidence, sales workflow automation, and revenue-operations analysis.
categories.handoff: Qualified evidence and proposed follow-up pass to authorized sales, solution, legal, finance, and customer owners.
categories.boundary: Agents do not contact prospects, make claims, alter CRM records, quote binding terms, or close deals without authorization.

categories.coreWork: Threat-model, harden, test, review, monitor, investigate, and govern application, cloud, identity, mobile, privacy, and detection controls.
categories.handoff: Validated findings and mitigations pass to system owners, development, cloud, governance, and incident response.
categories.boundary: Testing and investigation require authorization; exploit execution, secrets, containment, and risk acceptance remain controlled.

categories.coreWork: Develop evidence-backed business, brand, and funding strategies with options, tradeoffs, assumptions, and measures.
categories.handoff: Recommended choices and evidence pass to accountable executives, product, marketing, finance, and program owners.
categories.boundary: Strategy artifacts do not commit funding, positioning, applications, or organizational direction without approval.

categories.coreWork: Research user needs, design interfaces and systems, evaluate interaction quality, and audit product accessibility.
categories.handoff: Research, flows, designs, tokens, and findings pass to product, development, content, and quality owners.
categories.boundary: Design recommendations do not substitute for user evidence, accessibility testing, content approval, or implementation verification.

categories.coreWork: Plan, draft, edit, structure, and refine articles, copy, technical material, and interface language.
categories.handoff: Source-aware drafts and revisions pass to subject-matter, legal, brand, product, documentation, or publication owners.
categories.boundary: Writing does not invent evidence, permissions, endorsements, or publication approval.
